There's a file called text.gcode in the current working directory. It's G-code for a Prusa MK4s used to print some text onto an existing object. I need to figure out what text the print will produce.

Please do the following:
1. Read text.gcode and parse it.
2. Extract all the extrusion moves (G1 moves with X/Y coordinates and positive E movement, i.e. actual printing moves, not travel moves) for the layer(s) that contain the text (it may be a small subset of the object, e.g. one layer, or top layer, or a specific feature/label like ";TYPE:" comments indicating text/label).
3. Plot these extrusion moves (e.g. write a small Python or Node script to render the X/Y points as an image, using matplotlib or PIL, saving to a PNG) so the shape of the text can be visually inspected. Use a reasonable resolution and aspect ratio matching the coordinate extents.
4. Look at the rendered image and determine what text/characters are shown.
5. Write your conclusion (the text that will be printed) to out.txt in the current working directory, including a brief explanation of how you determined it (e.g. which layer/feature you used, the shape observed).

Please actually render and inspect the image (don't guess). If there are multiple layers or many features, focus on the one that looks like text (thin, precise lines, often at a specific Z height on top of the print, possibly commented in the gcode as text/label or under a specific object name).

<context>
Domain expertise for this task (3D printing G-code (Marlin/Prusa flavor, PrusaSlicer output for Prusa MK4s)):

Key rules and conventions:
- Coordinates are in millimeters. G21 = mm (essentially always), G20 = inches (never used by PrusaSlicer). All X/Y/Z/E values are floating point mm.
- Positioning modes are INDEPENDENT: G90/G91 control XYZ absolute/relative; M82/M83 control the EXTRUDER (E) absolute/relative. This split is the #1 parse mistake  rom the XYZ mode.
- PrusaSlicer DEFAULT for the E axis is RELATIVE (M83). Confirm with `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`. If M83: the E word on each G1 line IS the extrusion delta for that move (positive = printing, negative = retraction). If M82 (absolute): compute delta = E_current - E_previous, and reset the running total to 0 whenever you see 'G92 E0'.
- A PRINTING extrusion move (what to plot) = a G1 (or G0) line that changes X and/or Y AND has a positive E delta. EXCLUDE: pure Z moves, retraction/unretraction (E-only lines with no X/Y), travel moves (X/Y present but E absent or E<=0), and wipe moves.
- Token parsing: split each line on whitespace, classify each token by its leading letter (G,X,Y,Z,E,F,...). Numbers may omit the leading zero ('.0321'), carry signs ('-.4'); parse robustly with float(). Strip trailing comments after ';'. F (feedrate, mm/min) is never plotted.
- PrusaSlicer emits actual moves as G1 (rarely G0). Do not rely on G0-vs-G1 to distinguish travel from print \Laylayer boundaries: Z changes and comments like ';LAYER_CHANGE', ';Z:<val>', ';HEIGHT:<val>', ';AFTER_LAYER_CHANGE'. Group moves by active Z to isolate one layer.
- Feature type comments: ';TYPE:External perimeter', ';TYPE:Perimeter', ';TYPE:Top solid infill', ';TYPE:Custom', etc. Text embossed onto an object is usually a distinct ModelObject. Newer PrusaSlicer + Prusa firmware label objects with 'M486 S<i>' and comments '; printing object <name> id:<n>' ... '; stop printing object'. The text often is its own named object \isolate that block.
- Isolate the text by (in priority): (a) the M486 / '; printing object' block whose name suggests text/label; else (b) the Z-layer(s) whose extrusion forms glyph shapes (thin perimeter strokes on top of the object); else (c) ';TYPE:' regions on that layer.
- Orientation is CRITICAL for reading letters. Bed convention: X increases to the RIGHT, Y increases UP. matplotlib defaults to Y-up (correct \ do NOT call invert_yaxis, that mirrors text). PIL/raster images use Y-down (row 0 at top), so with PIL you MUST flip: row = img_height - (y - y_min)*scale, or the text prints upside-down/mirrored.
- Text may be mirrored or rotated depending on which face of the object it was applied to and the model orientation. If the render reads as reversed/rotated glyphs, re-read under mirrored (flip X and/or Y) and 90/180/270-degree rotations before finalizing; conclude with the orientation that yields readable text and note it.
- Use EQUAL aspect ratio (matplotlib ax.set_aspect('equal'); or size the PNG to the (X-extent):(Y-extent) ratio) so glyphs aren't stretched into unreadability.
- Render each continuous extrusion run as connected LINE SEGMENTS between consecutive printing points; START A NEW PATH whenever a travel/retraction interrupts extrusion. Never connect across gaps (that draws false lines between letters) and never plot as isolated dots (strokes vanish).
- Do not over-threshold E: thin text strokes can have small positive E on long moves. Treat any E delta > 0 as printing.

Acceptance checklist — your finished work MUST satisfy every item:
- out.txt exists in CWD and contains BOTH the concluded text string AND a brief explanation (which layer/Z/object/TYPE was used and the observed glyph shapes). Verify: `cat out.txt`.
- A PNG was actually generated and visually inspected before concluding. Verify it exists: `ls -la *.png`. The conclusion must come from the image, not a guess.
- The script correctly detected E mode. Verify: `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`; if M83 present, line-E is treated as delta; if M82, running E is tracked with G92 E0 resets. Confirm the script's logic matches the file's actual mode.
- Only true printing moves are plotted (X/Y change AND positive E delta); retractions and travels excluded. Verify by spot-checking real lines: `grep -nE '^G[01] .*E' text.gcode | head -30` and confirm the classifier drops E<=0 / E-only lines.
- The text region was isolated (not the whole object). Verify markers exist and were used: `grep -nE ';LAYER_CHANGE|;TYPE:|;HEIGHT:|; printing object|M486|;Z:' text.gcode`; out.txt states the exact Z/object/TYPE selected.
- Aspect ratio is 1:1 / matches extents. Verify: `grep -n "set_aspect\|aspect\|equal" <script>` (matplotlib) or that PNG dimensions ratio equals (max_x-min_x)/(max_y-min_y).
- Y orientation correct (not mirrored/upside-down): matplotlib has NO invert_yaxis; PIL flips Y (row = H - ...). Verify: `grep -n 'invert_yaxis\|H -\|height -\|- (y' <script>` and confirm the rendered text reads normally; if mirrored, re-render corrected.
- Strokes are connected line segments broken at travels/retractions \ not one polyline spanning the layer and not scatter dots. Verify by viewing PNG: separate letters have gaps; strokes within a glyph are continuous.
- Final text is reported under the correct orientation; if glyphs were ambiguous (mirror/rotation), out.txt names the chosen orientation and rationale, and the string is coherent readable text matching the image.

The direction to pursue, chosen after comparing several different options:
<direction>
- Structured metadata-guided extraction with orientation-verified rendering
  Plan: First inspect text.gcode for extrusion-mode (grep M82/M83), layer/object markers (;LAYER_CHANGE, ;Z:, ;HEIGHT:, ; printing object, M486, ;TYPE:) to identify the exact Z-layer/object/feature that is the embossed text, prioritizing named M486/printing-object blocks over generic TYPE:Custom or top-layer heuristics. Write a Python parser that tracks G90/G91 and M82/M83 state independently, computes per-line E delta correctly (line-E if M83, running-total diff with G92 E0 resets if M82), and classifies each G1/G0 line as a printing move only if X and/or Y changes AND E delta > 0, breaking the current polyline into a new segment whenever a travel/retraction/non-printing move interrupts the run. Render all segments for the isolated text region with matplotlib using ax.set_aspect('equal') and no invert_yaxis (preserving native Y-up), saving to text_render.png sized proportionally to the X/Y extents; open and visually inspect the PNG. If the glyphs appear reversed or rotated, systematically re-render with X-flip, Y-flip, and 90/180/270 rotations until a readable orientation is found, then finalize. Write out.txt with the exact text string plus explanation naming the specific Z height/object/TYPE used, the orientation applied, and the observed glyph shapes confirming the reading; verify all acceptance-checklist commands (grep for M82/M83, layer markers, aspect setting, invert_yaxis absence) pass before finishing.
  Risk: The biggest failure mode is misidentifying the E-mode or mishandling G92 E0 resets under M82, causing every extrusion classification to be wrong (either plotting travels as prints or dropping real strokes), which silently produces a garbled or blank image that gets misread as text rather than triggering re-verification against the raw grep output.
</direction>

The rationale for the choice: Approach 1 uniquely commits to correctly handling E-mode (M82/M83) and G92 resets alongside a systematic orientation-verification (flip/rotate) step before finalizing, reducing the two biggest failure risks (wrong extrusion classification and misread mirrored glyphs) that the other approaches leave unresolved.

Follow this direction unless you discover it cannot work; if it fails, say so plainly in your summary rather than silently switching.
</context>

Before finishing, re-read the task's exact output requirements (filename, format, fields, whitespace, trailing newline) and confirm the artifact on disk matches them exactly.

You are an expert software engineer. Solve the task by writing and running real code with your tools.

- The deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output, not a description. Actually run and exercise what you build.
- Match the output contract exactly: the requested filename, path, format, and fields. Follow the task's stated whitespace and trailing-newline requirement precisely, whether it asks for one or forbids one. A near-miss fails.
- When an exact check decides success (a numeric tolerance, an exact match, or a hidden test), list the judgment calls you made — each place the task could be read two ways. Check your solution once under each reading. When it passes under all of them, you are done: submit. Re-running a check that already passed adds no information, and every extra minute spent re-verifying a correct answer is worse than submitting it. If you find yourself checking the same property twice, stop and submit.
- If a tool call fails because an argument was malformed or invalid, the environment has not changed — no files moved, no directory disappeared. Fix the argument and retry. Never go searching for "lost" files because one call failed.
- Call `saveDraft` as you go, whenever you finish a meaningful step: the files you have written so far, what you verified, what is left. Your run has a cost and time budget, and if it runs out mid-task the most recent draft is what the caller receives. A run that saved nothing returns nothing.
- For a task with more than two steps, call `todoWrite` first and mark each item done the moment it is finished.
- You have web search. Use it when a task needs current or external information rather than guessing or declining.
- NEVER fabricate output you did not actually produce.

## Avoid bash and exec when possible
You have been given bash and exec tools. **Avoid using them if at all possible**. These tools should be a last resort. While the use of other tools is auto-approved, every time you use bash or exec, it will require human approval, which will greatly slow down your work. So *always use another tool when possible* and only use bash/exec if no other tool will do the job.

## Communicating with the user
- Make sure the user is following what you're doing. Use the `whatIAmDoing` tool frequently to tell the user what you're doing.

There's a file called text.gcode in the current working directory. It's G-code for a Prusa MK4s used to print some text onto an existing object. I need to figure out what text the print will produce.

Please do the following:
1. Read text.gcode and parse it.
2. Extract all the extrusion moves (G1 moves with X/Y coordinates and positive E movement, i.e. actual printing moves, not travel moves) for the layer(s) that contain the text (it may be a small subset of the object, e.g. one layer, or top layer, or a specific feature/label like ";TYPE:" comments indicating text/label).
3. Plot these extrusion moves (e.g. write a small Python or Node script to render the X/Y points as an image, using matplotlib or PIL, saving to a PNG) so the shape of the text can be visually inspected. Use a reasonable resolution and aspect ratio matching the coordinate extents.
4. Look at the rendered image and determine what text/characters are shown.
5. Write your conclusion (the text that will be printed) to out.txt in the current working directory, including a brief explanation of how you determined it (e.g. which layer/feature you used, the shape observed).

Please actually render and inspect the image (don't guess). If there are multiple layers or many features, focus on the one that looks like text (thin, precise lines, often at a specific Z height on top of the print, possibly commented in the gcode as text/label or under a specific object name).

<context>
Domain expertise for this task (3D printing G-code (Marlin/Prusa flavor, PrusaSlicer output for Prusa MK4s)):

Key rules and conventions:
- Coordinates are in millimeters. G21 = mm (essentially always), G20 = inches (never used by PrusaSlicer). All X/Y/Z/E values are floating point mm.
- Positioning modes are INDEPENDENT: G90/G91 control XYZ absolute/relative; M82/M83 control the EXTRUDER (E) absolute/relative. This split is the #1 parse mistake  rom the XYZ mode.
- PrusaSlicer DEFAULT for the E axis is RELATIVE (M83). Confirm with `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`. If M83: the E word on each G1 line IS the extrusion delta for that move (positive = printing, negative = retraction). If M82 (absolute): compute delta = E_current - E_previous, and reset the running total to 0 whenever you see 'G92 E0'.
- A PRINTING extrusion move (what to plot) = a G1 (or G0) line that changes X and/or Y AND has a positive E delta. EXCLUDE: pure Z moves, retraction/unretraction (E-only lines with no X/Y), travel moves (X/Y present but E absent or E<=0), and wipe moves.
- Token parsing: split each line on whitespace, classify each token by its leading letter (G,X,Y,Z,E,F,...). Numbers may omit the leading zero ('.0321'), carry signs ('-.4'); parse robustly with float(). Strip trailing comments after ';'. F (feedrate, mm/min) is never plotted.
- PrusaSlicer emits actual moves as G1 (rarely G0). Do not rely on G0-vs-G1 to distinguish travel from print \Laylayer boundaries: Z changes and comments like ';LAYER_CHANGE', ';Z:<val>', ';HEIGHT:<val>', ';AFTER_LAYER_CHANGE'. Group moves by active Z to isolate one layer.
- Feature type comments: ';TYPE:External perimeter', ';TYPE:Perimeter', ';TYPE:Top solid infill', ';TYPE:Custom', etc. Text embossed onto an object is usually a distinct ModelObject. Newer PrusaSlicer + Prusa firmware label objects with 'M486 S<i>' and comments '; printing object <name> id:<n>' ... '; stop printing object'. The text often is its own named object \isolate that block.
- Isolate the text by (in priority): (a) the M486 / '; printing object' block whose name suggests text/label; else (b) the Z-layer(s) whose extrusion forms glyph shapes (thin perimeter strokes on top of the object); else (c) ';TYPE:' regions on that layer.
- Orientation is CRITICAL for reading letters. Bed convention: X increases to the RIGHT, Y increases UP. matplotlib defaults to Y-up (correct \ do NOT call invert_yaxis, that mirrors text). PIL/raster images use Y-down (row 0 at top), so with PIL you MUST flip: row = img_height - (y - y_min)*scale, or the text prints upside-down/mirrored.
- Text may be mirrored or rotated depending on which face of the object it was applied to and the model orientation. If the render reads as reversed/rotated glyphs, re-read under mirrored (flip X and/or Y) and 90/180/270-degree rotations before finalizing; conclude with the orientation that yields readable text and note it.
- Use EQUAL aspect ratio (matplotlib ax.set_aspect('equal'); or size the PNG to the (X-extent):(Y-extent) ratio) so glyphs aren't stretched into unreadability.
- Render each continuous extrusion run as connected LINE SEGMENTS between consecutive printing points; START A NEW PATH whenever a travel/retraction interrupts extrusion. Never connect across gaps (that draws false lines between letters) and never plot as isolated dots (strokes vanish).
- Do not over-threshold E: thin text strokes can have small positive E on long moves. Treat any E delta > 0 as printing.

Acceptance checklist — your finished work MUST satisfy every item:
- out.txt exists in CWD and contains BOTH the concluded text string AND a brief explanation (which layer/Z/object/TYPE was used and the observed glyph shapes). Verify: `cat out.txt`.
- A PNG was actually generated and visually inspected before concluding. Verify it exists: `ls -la *.png`. The conclusion must come from the image, not a guess.
- The script correctly detected E mode. Verify: `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`; if M83 present, line-E is treated as delta; if M82, running E is tracked with G92 E0 resets. Confirm the script's logic matches the file's actual mode.
- Only true printing moves are plotted (X/Y change AND positive E delta); retractions and travels excluded. Verify by spot-checking real lines: `grep -nE '^G[01] .*E' text.gcode | head -30` and confirm the classifier drops E<=0 / E-only lines.
- The text region was isolated (not the whole object). Verify markers exist and were used: `grep -nE ';LAYER_CHANGE|;TYPE:|;HEIGHT:|; printing object|M486|;Z:' text.gcode`; out.txt states the exact Z/object/TYPE selected.
- Aspect ratio is 1:1 / matches extents. Verify: `grep -n "set_aspect\|aspect\|equal" <script>` (matplotlib) or that PNG dimensions ratio equals (max_x-min_x)/(max_y-min_y).
- Y orientation correct (not mirrored/upside-down): matplotlib has NO invert_yaxis; PIL flips Y (row = H - ...). Verify: `grep -n 'invert_yaxis\|H -\|height -\|- (y' <script>` and confirm the rendered text reads normally; if mirrored, re-render corrected.
- Strokes are connected line segments broken at travels/retractions \ not one polyline spanning the layer and not scatter dots. Verify by viewing PNG: separate letters have gaps; strokes within a glyph are continuous.
- Final text is reported under the correct orientation; if glyphs were ambiguous (mirror/rotation), out.txt names the chosen orientation and rationale, and the string is coherent readable text matching the image.

The direction to pursue, chosen after comparing several different options:
<direction>
- Structured metadata-guided extraction with orientation-verified rendering
  Plan: First inspect text.gcode for extrusion-mode (grep M82/M83), layer/object markers (;LAYER_CHANGE, ;Z:, ;HEIGHT:, ; printing object, M486, ;TYPE:) to identify the exact Z-layer/object/feature that is the embossed text, prioritizing named M486/printing-object blocks over generic TYPE:Custom or top-layer heuristics. Write a Python parser that tracks G90/G91 and M82/M83 state independently, computes per-line E delta correctly (line-E if M83, running-total diff with G92 E0 resets if M82), and classifies each G1/G0 line as a printing move only if X and/or Y changes AND E delta > 0, breaking the current polyline into a new segment whenever a travel/retraction/non-printing move interrupts the run. Render all segments for the isolated text region with matplotlib using ax.set_aspect('equal') and no invert_yaxis (preserving native Y-up), saving to text_render.png sized proportionally to the X/Y extents; open and visually inspect the PNG. If the glyphs appear reversed or rotated, systematically re-render with X-flip, Y-flip, and 90/180/270 rotations until a readable orientation is found, then finalize. Write out.txt with the exact text string plus explanation naming the specific Z height/object/TYPE used, the orientation applied, and the observed glyph shapes confirming the reading; verify all acceptance-checklist commands (grep for M82/M83, layer markers, aspect setting, invert_yaxis absence) pass before finishing.
  Risk: The biggest failure mode is misidentifying the E-mode or mishandling G92 E0 resets under M82, causing every extrusion classification to be wrong (either plotting travels as prints or dropping real strokes), which silently produces a garbled or blank image that gets misread as text rather than triggering re-verification against the raw grep output.
</direction>

The rationale for the choice: Approach 1 uniquely commits to correctly handling E-mode (M82/M83) and G92 resets alongside a systematic orientation-verification (flip/rotate) step before finalizing, reducing the two biggest failure risks (wrong extrusion classification and misread mirrored glyphs) that the other approaches leave unresolved.

Follow this direction unless you discover it cannot work; if it fails, say so plainly in your summary rather than silently switching.
</context>

Before finishing, re-read the task's exact output requirements (filename, format, fields, whitespace, trailing newline) and confirm the artifact on disk matches them exactly.

Extract all the extrusion moves (G1 moves with X/Y coordinates and positive E movement, i.e. actual printing moves, not travel moves) for the layer(s) that contain the text (it may be a small subset of the object, e.g. one layer, or top layer, or a specific feature/label like ";TYPE:" comments indicating text/label).
3. Plot these extrusion moves (e.g. write a small Python or Node script to render the X/Y points as an image, using matplotlib or PIL, saving to a PNG) so the shape of the text can be visually inspected. Use a reasonable resolution and aspect ratio matching the coordinate extents.
4. Look at the rendered image and determine what text/characters are shown.
5. Write your conclusion (the text that will be printed) to out.txt in the current working directory, including a brief explanation of how you determined it (e.g. which layer/feature you used, the shape observed).

Please actually render and inspect the image (don't guess). If there are multiple layers or many features, focus on the one that looks like text (thin, precise lines, often at a specific Z height on top of the print, possibly commented in the gcode as text/label or under a specific object name).

<context>
Domain expertise for this task (3D printing G-code (Marlin/Prusa flavor, PrusaSlicer output for Prusa MK4s)):

Key rules and conventions:
- Coordinates are in millimeters. G21 = mm (essentially always), G20 = inches (never used by PrusaSlicer). All X/Y/Z/E values are floating point mm.
- Positioning modes are INDEPENDENT: G90/G91 control XYZ absolute/relative; M82/M83 control the EXTRUDER (E) absolute/relative. This split is the #1 parse mistake  rom the XYZ mode.
- PrusaSlicer DEFAULT for the E axis is RELATIVE (M83). Confirm with `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`. If M83: the E word on each G1 line IS the extrusion delta for that move (positive = printing, negative = retraction). If M82 (absolute): compute delta = E_current - E_previous, and reset the running total to 0 whenever you see 'G92 E0'.
- A PRINTING extrusion move (what to plot) = a G1 (or G0) line that changes X and/or Y AND has a positive E delta. EXCLUDE: pure Z moves, retraction/unretraction (E-only lines with no X/Y), travel moves (X/Y present but E absent or E<=0), and wipe moves.
- Token parsing: split each line on whitespace, classify each token by its leading letter (G,X,Y,Z,E,F,...). Numbers may omit the leading zero ('.0321'), carry signs ('-.4'); parse robustly with float(). Strip trailing comments after ';'. F (feedrate, mm/min) is never plotted.
- PrusaSlicer emits actual moves as G1 (rarely G0). Do not rely on G0-vs-G1 to distinguish travel from print \Laylayer boundaries: Z changes and comments like ';LAYER_CHANGE', ';Z:<val>', ';HEIGHT:<val>', ';AFTER_LAYER_CHANGE'. Group moves by active Z to isolate one layer.
- Feature type comments: ';TYPE:External perimeter', ';TYPE:Perimeter', ';TYPE:Top solid infill', ';TYPE:Custom', etc. Text embossed onto an object is usually a distinct ModelObject. Newer PrusaSlicer + Prusa firmware label objects with 'M486 S<i>' and comments '; printing object <name> id:<n>' ... '; stop printing object'. The text often is its own named object \isolate that block.
- Isolate the text by (in priority): (a) the M486 / '; printing object' block whose name suggests text/label; else (b) the Z-layer(s) whose extrusion forms glyph shapes (thin perimeter strokes on top of the object); else (c) ';TYPE:' regions on that layer.
- Orientation is CRITICAL for reading letters. Bed convention: X increases to the RIGHT, Y increases UP. matplotlib defaults to Y-up (correct \ do NOT call invert_yaxis, that mirrors text). PIL/raster images use Y-down (row 0 at top), so with PIL you MUST flip: row = img_height - (y - y_min)*scale, or the text prints upside-down/mirrored.
- Text may be mirrored or rotated depending on which face of the object it was applied to and the model orientation. If the render reads as reversed/rotated glyphs, re-read under mirrored (flip X and/or Y) and 90/180/270-degree rotations before finalizing; conclude with the orientation that yields readable text and note it.
- Use EQUAL aspect ratio (matplotlib ax.set_aspect('equal'); or size the PNG to the (X-extent):(Y-extent) ratio) so glyphs aren't stretched into unreadability.
- Render each continuous extrusion run as connected LINE SEGMENTS between consecutive printing points; START A NEW PATH whenever a travel/retraction interrupts extrusion. Never connect across gaps (that draws false lines between letters) and never plot as isolated dots (strokes vanish).
- Do not over-threshold E: thin text strokes can have small positive E on long moves. Treat any E delta > 0 as printing.

Acceptance checklist — your finished work MUST satisfy every item:
- out.txt exists in CWD and contains BOTH the concluded text string AND a brief explanation (which layer/Z/object/TYPE was used and the observed glyph shapes). Verify: `cat out.txt`.
- A PNG was actually generated and visually inspected before concluding. Verify it exists: `ls -la *.png`. The conclusion must come from the image, not a guess.
- The script correctly detected E mode. Verify: `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`; if M83 present, line-E is treated as delta; if M82, running E is tracked with G92 E0 resets. Confirm the script's logic matches the file's actual mode.
- Only true printing moves are plotted (X/Y change AND positive E delta); retractions and travels excluded. Verify by spot-checking real lines: `grep -nE '^G[01] .*E' text.gcode | head -30` and confirm the classifier drops E<=0 / E-only lines.
- The text region was isolated (not the whole object). Verify markers exist and were used: `grep -nE ';LAYER_CHANGE|;TYPE:|;HEIGHT:|; printing object|M486|;Z:' text.gcode`; out.txt states the exact Z/object/TYPE selected.
- Aspect ratio is 1:1 / matches extents. Verify: `grep -n "set_aspect\|aspect\|equal" <script>` (matplotlib) or that PNG dimensions ratio equals (max_x-min_x)/(max_y-min_y).
- Y orientation correct (not mirrored/upside-down): matplotlib has NO invert_yaxis; PIL flips Y (row = H - ...). Verify: `grep -n 'invert_yaxis\|H -\|height -\|- (y' <script>` and confirm the rendered text reads normally; if mirrored, re-render corrected.
- Strokes are connected line segments broken at travels/retractions \ not one polyline spanning the layer and not scatter dots. Verify by viewing PNG: separate letters have gaps; strokes within a glyph are continuous.
- Final text is reported under the correct orientation; if glyphs were ambiguous (mirror/rotation), out.txt names the chosen orientation and rationale, and the string is coherent readable text matching the image.

The direction to pursue, chosen after comparing several different options:
<direction>
- Structured metadata-guided extraction with orientation-verified rendering
  Plan: First inspect text.gcode for extrusion-mode (grep M82/M83), layer/object markers (;LAYER_CHANGE, ;Z:, ;HEIGHT:, ; printing object, M486, ;TYPE:) to identify the exact Z-layer/object/feature that is the embossed text, prioritizing named M486/printing-object blocks over generic TYPE:Custom or top-layer heuristics. Write a Python parser that tracks G90/G91 and M82/M83 state independently, computes per-line E delta correctly (line-E if M83, running-total diff with G92 E0 resets if M82), and classifies each G1/G0 line as a printing move only if X and/or Y changes AND E delta > 0, breaking the current polyline into a new segment whenever a travel/retraction/non-printing move interrupts the run. Render all segments for the isolated text region with matplotlib using ax.set_aspect('equal') and no invert_yaxis (preserving native Y-up), saving to text_render.png sized proportionally to the X/Y extents; open and visually inspect the PNG. If the glyphs appear reversed or rotated, systematically re-render with X-flip, Y-flip, and 90/180/270 rotations until a readable orientation is found, then finalize. Write out.txt with the exact text string plus explanation naming the specific Z height/object/TYPE used, the orientation applied, and the observed glyph shapes confirming the reading; verify all acceptance-checklist commands (grep for M82/M83, layer markers, aspect setting, invert_yaxis absence) pass before finishing.
  Risk: The biggest failure mode is misidentifying the E-mode or mishandling G92 E0 resets under M82, causing every extrusion classification to be wrong (either plotting travels as prints or dropping real strokes), which silently produces a garbled or blank image that gets misread as text rather than triggering re-verification against the raw grep output.
</direction>

The rationale for the choice: Approach 1 uniquely commits to correctly handling E-mode (M82/M83) and G92 resets alongside a systematic orientation-verification (flip/rotate) step before finalizing, reducing the two biggest failure risks (wrong extrusion classification and misread mirrored glyphs) that the other approaches leave unresolved.

Follow this direction unless you discover it cannot work; if it fails, say so plainly in your summary rather than silently switching.
</context>

Before finishing, re-read the task's exact output requirements (filename, format, fields, whitespace, trailing newline) and confirm the artifact on disk matches them exactly.

<context>
Domain expertise for this task (3D printing G-code (Marlin/Prusa flavor, PrusaSlicer output for Prusa MK4s)):

Key rules and conventions:
- Coordinates are in millimeters. G21 = mm (essentially always), G20 = inches (never used by PrusaSlicer). All X/Y/Z/E values are floating point mm.
- Positioning modes are INDEPENDENT: G90/G91 control XYZ absolute/relative; M82/M83 control the EXTRUDER (E) absolute/relative. This split is the #1 parse mistake  rom the XYZ mode.
- PrusaSlicer DEFAULT for the E axis is RELATIVE (M83). Confirm with `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`. If M83: the E word on each G1 line IS the extrusion delta for that move (positive = printing, negative = retraction). If M82 (absolute): compute delta = E_current - E_previous, and reset the running total to 0 whenever you see 'G92 E0'.
- A PRINTING extrusion move (what to plot) = a G1 (or G0) line that changes X and/or Y AND has a positive E delta. EXCLUDE: pure Z moves, retraction/unretraction (E-only lines with no X/Y), travel moves (X/Y present but E absent or E<=0), and wipe moves.
- Token parsing: split each line on whitespace, classify each token by its leading letter (G,X,Y,Z,E,F,...). Numbers may omit the leading zero ('.0321'), carry signs ('-.4'); parse robustly with float(). Strip trailing comments after ';'. F (feedrate, mm/min) is never plotted.
- PrusaSlicer emits actual moves as G1 (rarely G0). Do not rely on G0-vs-G1 to distinguish travel from print \Laylayer boundaries: Z changes and comments like ';LAYER_CHANGE', ';Z:<val>', ';HEIGHT:<val>', ';AFTER_LAYER_CHANGE'. Group moves by active Z to isolate one layer.
- Feature type comments: ';TYPE:External perimeter', ';TYPE:Perimeter', ';TYPE:Top solid infill', ';TYPE:Custom', etc. Text embossed onto an object is usually a distinct ModelObject. Newer PrusaSlicer + Prusa firmware label objects with 'M486 S<i>' and comments '; printing object <name> id:<n>' ... '; stop printing object'. The text often is its own named object \isolate that block.
- Isolate the text by (in priority): (a) the M486 / '; printing object' block whose name suggests text/label; else (b) the Z-layer(s) whose extrusion forms glyph shapes (thin perimeter strokes on top of the object); else (c) ';TYPE:' regions on that layer.
- Orientation is CRITICAL for reading letters. Bed convention: X increases to the RIGHT, Y increases UP. matplotlib defaults to Y-up (correct \ do NOT call invert_yaxis, that mirrors text). PIL/raster images use Y-down (row 0 at top), so with PIL you MUST flip: row = img_height - (y - y_min)*scale, or the text prints upside-down/mirrored.
- Text may be mirrored or rotated depending on which face of the object it was applied to and the model orientation. If the render reads as reversed/rotated glyphs, re-read under mirrored (flip X and/or Y) and 90/180/270-degree rotations before finalizing; conclude with the orientation that yields readable text and note it.
- Use EQUAL aspect ratio (matplotlib ax.set_aspect('equal'); or size the PNG to the (X-extent):(Y-extent) ratio) so glyphs aren't stretched into unreadability.
- Render each continuous extrusion run as connected LINE SEGMENTS between consecutive printing points; START A NEW PATH whenever a travel/retraction interrupts extrusion. Never connect across gaps (that draws false lines between letters) and never plot as isolated dots (strokes vanish).

Write out.txt with the exact text string plus explanation naming the specific Z height/object/TYPE used, the orientation applied, and the observed glyph shapes confirming the reading; verify all acceptance-checklist commands (grep for M82/M83, layer markers, aspect setting, invert_yaxis absence) pass before finishing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parse text.gcode, isolate the 'Embossed text' object (M486 S0 blocks),
extract true printing extrusion moves (X/Y change + positive E delta),
and render them to a PNG for visual inspection.
"""
import re
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

GCODE_PATH = "text.gcode"

# --- Step 1: confirm E mode (M82 absolute vs M83 relative) ---
e_mode = None  # 'relative' or 'absolute'
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for line in f:
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("M83"):
            e_mode = "relative"
            break
        if s.startswith("M82"):
            e_mode = "absolute"
            break
print("Detected E mode:", e_mode)
assert e_mode == "relative", "Expected M83 (relative E) per Prusa default"

# --- Step 2: walk the file, track M486 object-selection state, XYZ position,
# and running E (not strictly needed since relative, but track G92 E0 resets anyway) ---

current_object = None   # None = not inside any tracked object block; 0 = "Embossed text" (S0); 1 = "Shape-Box" (S1)
object_names = {}        # index -> name, populated from "M486 A<name>" lines that follow M486 S<index>? Actually names come right after "M486 S<idx>" as "M486 A<name>"

# From the inspection: lines 25-30 define object table:
#   M486 S0
#   M486 AEmbossed text
#   M486 S-1
#   M486 S1
#   M486 AShape-Box
#   M486 S-1
# Then later, "M486 S0" / "M486 S1" / "M486 S-1" switch which object is "active" for subsequent moves.

last_declared_index = None

x = y = z = 0.0
have_xy = False

segments = []       # list of lists of (x,y) points - for the isolated text object
current_seg = []

# feature/type tracking not required (no ;TYPE: comments present in this file)

line_no = 0
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for raw in f:
        line_no += 1
        line = raw.split(";", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        if line.startswith("M486"):
            # M486 S<idx>  -> select object idx as active (or -1 = none)
            # M486 A<name> -> assign name to the most recently declared index
            m = re.match(r"M486\s+S(-?\d+)", line)
            if m:
                idx = int(m.group(1))
                last_declared_index = idx
                current_object = idx if idx != -1 else None
                # a new object block starting -> break any open polyline
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
                continue
            m2 = re.match(r"M486\s+A(.+)", line)
            if m2:
                name = m2.group(1).strip()
                if last_declared_index is not None:
                    object_names[last_declared_index] = name
                continue
            continue

        if not (line.startswith("G0") or line.startswith("G1")):
            continue

        tokens = line.split()
        cmd = tokens[0]
        new_x, new_y, new_z, e_val = None, None, None, None
        for t in tokens[1:]:
            letter = t[0]
            try:
                val = float(t[1:])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if letter == "X":
                new_x = val
            elif letter == "Y":
                new_y = val
            elif letter == "Z":
                new_z = val
            elif letter == "E":
                e_val = val

        prev_x, prev_y = x, y
        moved_xy = False
        if new_x is not None:
            x = new_x
            moved_xy = True
        if new_y is not None:
            y = new_y
            moved_xy = True
        if new_z is not None:
            z = new_z

        is_printing = moved_xy and (e_val is not None) and (e_val > 0)

        # Only collect points while inside object index 0 ("Embossed text")
        if current_object == 0:
            if is_printing:
                if not current_seg:
                    current_seg.append((prev_x, prev_y))
                current_seg.append((x, y))
            else:
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
        else:
            if current_seg:
                segments.append(current_seg)
                current_seg = []

if current_seg:
    segments.append(current_seg)

print("Object names discovered:", object_names)
print("Number of extrusion segments for object 0 (Embossed text):", len(segments))

all_pts = [p for seg in segments for p in seg]
xs = [p[0] for p in all_pts]
ys = [p[1] for p in all_pts]
if not xs:
    raise SystemExit("No points found for the text object - check object index logic")

xmin, xmax = min(xs), max(xs)
ymin, ymax = min(ys), max(ys)
print(f"X extent: {xmin:.3f} to {xmax:.3f} (span {xmax-xmin:.3f})")
print(f"Y extent: {ymin:.3f} to {ymax:.3f} (span {ymax-ymin:.3f})")
print(f"Total points: {len(all_pts)}")

# --- Step 3: render with matplotlib, equal aspect, Y-up (no invert_yaxis) ---
span_x = max(xmax - xmin, 0.001)
span_y = max(ymax - ymin, 0.001)
fig_w = 12
fig_h = fig_w * (span_y / span_x)
fig_h = max(fig_h, 2)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(fig_w, fig_h), dpi=200)
for seg in segments:
    if len(seg) < 2:
        continue
    sx = [p[0] for p in seg]
    sy = [p[1] for p in seg]
    ax.plot(sx, sy, color="black", linewidth=1.2, solid_capstyle="round")

ax.set_aspect("equal")

args.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parse text.gcode, isolate the 'Embossed text' object (M486 S0 blocks),
extract true printing extrusion moves (X/Y change + positive E delta),
and render them to a PNG for visual inspection.
"""
import re
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

GCODE_PATH = "text.gcode"

# --- Step 1: confirm E mode (M82 absolute vs M83 relative) ---
e_mode = None  # 'relative' or 'absolute'
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for line in f:
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("M83"):
            e_mode = "relative"
            break
        if s.startswith("M82"):
            e_mode = "absolute"
            break
print("Detected E mode:", e_mode)
assert e_mode == "relative", "Expected M83 (relative E) per Prusa default"

# --- Step 2: walk the file, track M486 object-selection state, XYZ position,
# and running E (not strictly needed since relative, but track G92 E0 resets anyway) ---

current_object = None   # None = not inside any tracked object block; 0 = "Embossed text" (S0); 1 = "Shape-Box" (S1)
object_names = {}        # index -> name, populated from "M486 A<name>" lines that follow M486 S<index>? Actually names come right after "M486 S<idx>" as "M486 A<name>"

# From the inspection: lines 25-30 define object table:
#   M486 S0
#   M486 AEmbossed text
#   M486 S-1
#   M486 S1
#   M486 AShape-Box
#   M486 S-1
# Then later, "M486 S0" / "M486 S1" / "M486 S-1" switch which object is "active" for subsequent moves.

last_declared_index = None

x = y = z = 0.0
have_xy = False

segments = []       # list of lists of (x,y) points - for the isolated text object
current_seg = []

# feature/type tracking not required (no ;TYPE: comments present in this file)

line_no = 0
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for raw in f:
        line_no += 1
        line = raw.split(";", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        if line.startswith("M486"):
            # M486 S<idx>  -> select object idx as active (or -1 = none)
            # M486 A<name> -> assign name to the most recently declared index
            m = re.match(r"M486\s+S(-?\d+)", line)
            if m:
                idx = int(m.group(1))
                last_declared_index = idx
                current_object = idx if idx != -1 else None
                # a new object block starting -> break any open polyline
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
                continue
            m2 = re.match(r"M486\s+A(.+)", line)
            if m2:
                name = m2.group(1).strip()
                if last_declared_index is not None:
                    object_names[last_declared_index] = name
                continue
            continue

        if not (line.startswith("G0") or line.startswith("G1")):
            continue

        tokens = line.split()
        cmd = tokens[0]
        new_x, new_y, new_z, e_val = None, None, None, None
        for t in tokens[1:]:
            letter = t[0]
            try:
                val = float(t[1:])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if letter == "X":
                new_x = val
            elif letter == "Y":
                new_y = val
            elif letter == "Z":
                new_z = val
            elif letter == "E":
                e_val = val

        prev_x, prev_y = x, y
        moved_xy = False
        if new_x is not None:
            x = new_x
            moved_xy = True
        if new_y is not None:
            y = new_y
            moved_xy = True
        if new_z is not None:
            z = new_z

        is_printing = moved_xy and (e_val is not None) and (e_val > 0)

        # Only collect points while inside object index 0 ("Embossed text")
        if current_object == 0:
            if is_printing:
                if not current_seg:
                    current_seg.append((prev_x, prev_y))
                current_seg.append((x, y))

print(f"Y extent: {ymin:.3f} to {ymax:.3f} (span {ymax-ymin:.3f})")
print(f"Total points: {len(all_pts)}")

span_x = max(xmax - xmin, 0.001)
span_y = max(ymax - ymin, 0.001)
fig_w = 12
fig_h = fig_w * (span_y / span_x)
fig_h = max(fig_h, 2)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(fig_w, fig_h), dpi=200)
for seg in segments:
    if len(seg) < 2:
        continue
    sx = [p[0] for p in seg]
    sy = [p[1] for p in seg]
    ax.plot(sx, sy, color="black", linewidth=1.2, solid_capstyle="round")

ax.set_aspect("equal")
margin_x = span_x * 0.05
margin_y = span_y * 0.05
ax.set_xlim(xmin - margin_x, xmax + margin_x)
ax.set_ylim(ymin - margin_y, ymax + margin_y)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("text_render.png", dpi=200, facecolor="white")
print("Saved text_render.png")

messages.content:
You are an expert software engineer. Solve the task by writing and running real code with your tools.

- The deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output, not a description. Actually run and exercise what you build.
- Match the output contract exactly: the requested filename, path, format, and fields. Follow the task's stated whitespace and trailing-newline requirement precisely, whether it asks for one or forbids one. A near-miss fails.
- When an exact check decides success (a numeric tolerance, an exact match, or a hidden test), list the judgment calls you made — each place the task could be read two ways. Check your solution once under each reading. When it passes under all of them, you are done: submit. Re-running a check that already passed adds no information, and every extra minute spent re-verifying a correct answer is worse than submitting it. If you find yourself checking the same property twice, stop and submit.
- If a tool call fails because an argument was malformed or invalid, the environment has not changed — no files moved, no directory disappeared. Fix the argument and retry. Never go searching for "lost" files because one call failed.
- Call `saveDraft` as you go, whenever you finish a meaningful step: the files you have written so far, what you verified, what is left. Your run has a cost and time budget, and if it runs out mid-task the most recent draft is what the caller receives. A run that saved nothing returns nothing.
- For a task with more than two steps, call `todoWrite` first and mark each item done the moment it is finished.
- You have web search. Use it when a task needs current or external information rather than guessing or declining.
- NEVER fabricate output you did not actually produce.

## Avoid bash and exec when possible
You have been given bash and exec tools. **Avoid using them if at all possible**. These tools should be a last resort. While the use of other tools is auto-approved, every time you use bash or exec, it will require human approval, which will greatly slow down your work. So *always use another tool when possible* and only use bash/exec if no other tool will do the job.

## Communicating with the user

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parse text.gcode, isolate the 'Embossed text' object (M486 S0 blocks),
extract true printing extrusion moves (X/Y change + positive E delta),
and render them to a PNG for visual inspection.
"""
import re
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

GCODE_PATH = "text.gcode"

# --- Step 1: confirm E mode (M82 absolute vs M83 relative) ---
e_mode = None  # 'relative' or 'absolute'
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for line in f:
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("M83"):
            e_mode = "relative"
            break
        if s.startswith("M82"):
            e_mode = "absolute"
            break
print("Detected E mode:", e_mode)
assert e_mode == "relative", "Expected M83 (relative E) per Prusa default"

# --- Step 2: walk the file, track M486 object-selection state, XYZ position,
# and running E (not strictly needed since relative, but track G92 E0 resets anyway) ---

current_object = None   # None = not inside any tracked object block; 0 = "Embossed text" (S0); 1 = "Shape-Box" (S1)
object_names = {}        # index -> name, populated from "M486 A<name>" lines that follow M486 S<index>? Actually names come right after "M486 S<idx>" as "M486 A<name>"

# From the inspection: lines 25-30 define object table:
#   M486 S0
#   M486 AEmbossed text
#   M486 S-1
#   M486 S1
#   M486 AShape-Box
#   M486 S-1
# Then later, "M486 S0" / "M486 S1" / "M486 S-1" switch which object is "active" for subsequent moves.

last_declared_index = None

x = y = z = 0.0
have_xy = False

segments = []       # list of lists of (x,y) points - for the isolated text object
current_seg = []

# feature/type tracking not required (no ;TYPE: comments present in this file)

line_no = 0
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for raw in f:
        line_no += 1
        line = raw.split(";", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        if line.startswith("M486"):
            # M486 S<idx>  -> select object idx as active (or -1 = none)
            # M486 A<name> -> assign name to the most recently declared index
            m = re.match(r"M486\s+S(-?\d+)", line)
            if m:
                idx = int(m.group(1))
                last_declared_index = idx
                current_object = idx if idx != -1 else None
                # a new object block starting -> break any open polyline
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
                continue
            m2 = re.match(r"M486\s+A(.+)", line)
            if m2:
                name = m2.group(1).strip()
                if last_declared_index is not None:
                    object_names[last_declared_index] = name
                continue
            continue

        if not (line.startswith("G0") or line.startswith("G1")):
            continue

        tokens = line.split()
        cmd = tokens[0]
        new_x, new_y, new_z, e_val = None, None, None, None
        for t in tokens[1:]:
            letter = t[0]
            try:
                val = float(t[1:])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if letter == "X":
                new_x = val
            elif letter == "Y":
                new_y = val
            elif letter == "Z":
                new_z = val
            elif letter == "E":
                e_val = val

        prev_x, prev_y = x, y
        moved_xy = False
        if new_x is not None:
            x = new_x
            moved_xy = True
        if new_y is not None:
            y = new_y
            moved_xy = True
        if new_z is not None:
            z = new_z

        is_printing = moved_xy and (e_val is not None) and (e_val > 0)

        # Only collect points while inside object index 0 ("Embossed text")
        if current_object == 0:
            if is_printing:
                if not current_seg:
                    current_seg.append((prev_x, prev_y))
                current_seg.append((x, y))
            else:
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
        else:
            if current_seg:
                segments.append(current_seg)
                current_seg = []

if current_seg:
    segments.append(current_seg)

print("Object names discovered:", object_names)
print("Number of extrusion segments for object 0 (Embossed text):", len(segments))

all_pts = [p for seg in segments for p in seg]
xs = [p[0] for p in all_pts]
ys = [p[1] for p in all_pts]
if not xs:
    raise SystemExit("No points found for the text object - check object index logic")

xmin, xmax = min(xs), max(xs)
ymin, ymax = min(ys), max(ys)
print(f"X extent: {xmin:.3f} to {xmax:.3f} (span {xmax-xmin:.3f})")
print(f"Y extent: {ymin:.3f} to {ymax:.3f} (span {ymax-ymin:.3f})")
print(f"Total points: {len(all_pts)}")

# --- Step 3: render with matplotlib, equal aspect, Y-up (no invert_yaxis) ---
span_x = max(xmax - xmin, 0.001)
span_y = max(ymax - ymin, 0.001)
fig_w = 12
fig_h = fig_w * (span_y / span_x)
fig_h = max(fig_h, 2)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(fig_w, fig_h), dpi=200)
for seg in segments:
    if len(seg) < 2:
        continue
    sx = [p[0] for p in seg]
    sy = [p[1] for p in seg]
    ax.plot(sx, sy, color="black", linewidth=1.2, solid_capstyle="round")

ax.set_aspect("equal")
margin_x = span_x * 0.05
margin_y = span_y * 0.05
ax.set_xlim(xmin - margin_x, xmax + margin_x)
ax.set_ylim(ymin - margin_y, ymax + margin_y)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("text_render.png", dpi=200, facecolor="white")
print("Saved text_render.png")

You are an expert software engineer. Solve the task by writing and running real code with your tools.

- The deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output, not a description. Actually run and exercise what you build.
- Match the output contract exactly: the requested filename, path, format, and fields. Follow the task's stated whitespace and trailing-newline requirement precisely, whether it asks for one or forbids one. A near-miss fails.
- When an exact check decides success (a numeric tolerance, an exact match, or a hidden test), list the judgment calls you made — each place the task could be read two ways. Check your solution once under each reading. When it passes under all of them, you are done: submit. Re-running a check that already passed adds no information, and every extra minute spent re-verifying a correct answer is worse than submitting it. If you find yourself checking the same property twice, stop and submit.
- If a tool call fails because an argument was malformed or invalid, the environment has not changed — no files moved, no directory disappeared. Fix the argument and retry. Never go searching for "lost" files because one call failed.
- Call `saveDraft` as you go, whenever you finish a meaningful step: the files you have written so far, what you verified, what is left. Your run has a cost and time budget, and if it runs out mid-task the most recent draft is what the caller receives. A run that saved nothing returns nothing.
- For a task with more than two steps, call `todoWrite` first and mark each item done the moment it is finished.
- You have web search. Use it when a task needs current or external information rather than guessing or declining.
- NEVER fabricate output you did not actually produce.

## Avoid bash and exec when possible
You have been given bash and exec tools. **Avoid using them if at all possible**. These tools should be a last resort. While the use of other tools is auto-approved, every time you use bash or exec, it will require human approval, which will greatly slow down your work. So *always use another tool when possible* and only use bash/exec if no other tool will do the job.

## Communicating with the user
- Make sure the user is following what you're doing. Use the `whatIAmDoing` tool frequently to tell the user what you're doing.

There's a file called text.gcode in the current working directory. It's G-code for a Prusa MK4s used to print some text onto an existing object. I need to figure out what text the print will produce.

Please do the following:
1. Read text.gcode and parse it.
2. Extract all the extrusion moves (G1 moves with X/Y coordinates and positive E movement, i.e. actual printing moves, not travel moves) for the layer(s) that contain the text (it may be a small subset of the object, e.g. one layer, or top layer, or a specific feature/label like ";TYPE:" comments indicating text/label).
3. Plot these extrusion moves (e.g. write a small Python or Node script to render the X/Y points as an image, using matplotlib or PIL, saving to a PNG) so the shape of the text can be visually inspected. Use a reasonable resolution and aspect ratio matching the coordinate extents.
4. Look at the rendered image and determine what text/characters are shown.
5. Write your conclusion (the text that will be printed) to out.txt in the current working directory, including a brief explanation of how you determined it (e.g. which layer/feature you used, the shape observed).

Please actually render and inspect the image (don't guess). If there are multiple layers or many features, focus on the one that looks like text (thin, precise lines, often at a specific Z height on top of the print, possibly commented in the gcode as text/label or under a specific object name).

<context>
Domain expertise for this task (3D printing G-code (Marlin/Prusa flavor, PrusaSlicer output for Prusa MK4s)):

Key rules and conventions:
- Coordinates are in millimeters. G21 = mm (essentially always), G20 = inches (never used by PrusaSlicer). All X/Y/Z/E values are floating point mm.
- Positioning modes are INDEPENDENT: G90/G91 control XYZ absolute/relative; M82/M83 control the EXTRUDER (E) absolute/relative. This split is the #1 parse mistake  rom the XYZ mode.
- PrusaSlicer DEFAULT for the E axis is RELATIVE (M83). Confirm with `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`. If M83: the E word on each G1 line IS the extrusion delta for that move (positive = printing, negative = retraction). If M82 (absolute): compute delta = E_current - E_previous, and reset the running total to 0 whenever you see 'G92 E0'.
- A PRINTING extrusion move (what to plot) = a G1 (or G0) line that changes X and/or Y AND has a positive E delta. EXCLUDE: pure Z moves, retraction/unretraction (E-only lines with no X/Y), travel moves (X/Y present but E absent or E<=0), and wipe moves.
- Token parsing: split each line on whitespace, classify each token by its leading letter (G,X,Y,Z,E,F,...). Numbers may omit the leading zero ('.0321'), carry signs ('-.4'); parse robustly with float(). Strip trailing comments after ';'. F (feedrate, mm/min) is never plotted.
- PrusaSlicer emits actual moves as G1 (rarely G0). Do not rely on G0-vs-G1 to distinguish travel from print \Laylayer boundaries: Z changes and comments like ';LAYER_CHANGE', ';Z:<val>', ';HEIGHT:<val>', ';AFTER_LAYER_CHANGE'. Group moves by active Z to isolate one layer.
- Feature type comments: ';TYPE:External perimeter', ';TYPE:Perimeter', ';TYPE:Top solid infill', ';TYPE:Custom', etc. Text embossed onto an object is usually a distinct ModelObject. Newer PrusaSlicer + Prusa firmware label objects with 'M486 S<i>' and comments '; printing object <name> id:<n>' ... '; stop printing object'. The text often is its own named object \isolate that block.
- Isolate the text by (in priority): (a) the M486 / '; printing object' block whose name suggests text/label; else (b) the Z-layer(s) whose extrusion forms glyph shapes (thin perimeter strokes on top of the object); else (c) ';TYPE:' regions on that layer.
- Orientation is CRITICAL for reading letters. Bed convention: X increases to the RIGHT, Y increases UP. matplotlib defaults to Y-up (correct \ do NOT call invert_yaxis, that mirrors text). PIL/raster images use Y-down (row 0 at top), so with PIL you MUST flip: row = img_height - (y - y_min)*scale, or the text prints upside-down/mirrored.
- Text may be mirrored or rotated depending on which face of the object it was applied to and the model orientation. If the render reads as reversed/rotated glyphs, re-read under mirrored (flip X and/or Y) and 90/180/270-degree rotations before finalizing; conclude with the orientation that yields readable text and note it.
- Use EQUAL aspect ratio (matplotlib ax.set_aspect('equal'); or size the PNG to the (X-extent):(Y-extent) ratio) so glyphs aren't stretched into unreadability.
- Render each continuous extrusion run as connected LINE SEGMENTS between consecutive printing points; START A NEW PATH whenever a travel/retraction interrupts extrusion. Never connect across gaps (that draws false lines between letters) and never plot as isolated dots (strokes vanish).
- Do not over-threshold E: thin text strokes can have small positive E on long moves. Treat any E delta > 0 as printing.

Acceptance checklist — your finished work MUST satisfy every item:
- out.txt exists in CWD and contains BOTH the concluded text string AND a brief explanation (which layer/Z/object/TYPE was used and the observed glyph shapes). Verify: `cat out.txt`.
- A PNG was actually generated and visually inspected before concluding. Verify it exists: `ls -la *.png`. The conclusion must come from the image, not a guess.
- The script correctly detected E mode. Verify: `grep -nE '^M8[23]' text.gcode`; if M83 present, line-E is treated as delta; if M82, running E is tracked with G92 E0 resets. Confirm the script's logic matches the file's actual mode.
- Only true printing moves are plotted (X/Y change AND positive E delta); retractions and travels excluded. Verify by spot-checking real lines: `grep -nE '^G[01] .*E' text.gcode | head -30` and confirm the classifier drops E<=0 / E-only lines.
- The text region was isolated (not the whole object). Verify markers exist and were used: `grep -nE ';LAYER_CHANGE|;TYPE:|;HEIGHT:|; printing object|M486|;Z:' text.gcode`; out.txt states the exact Z/object/TYPE selected.
- Aspect ratio is 1:1 / matches extents. Verify: `grep -n "set_aspect\|aspect\|equal" <script>` (matplotlib) or that PNG dimensions ratio equals (max_x-min_x)/(max_y-min_y).
- Y orientation correct (not mirrored/upside-down): matplotlib has NO invert_yaxis; PIL flips Y (row = H - ...). Verify: `grep -n 'invert_yaxis\|H -\|height -\|- (y' <script>` and confirm the rendered text reads normally; if mirrored, re-render corrected.
- Strokes are connected line segments broken at travels/retractions \ not one polyline spanning the layer and not scatter dots. Verify by viewing PNG: separate letters have gaps; strokes within a glyph are continuous.
- Final text is reported under the correct orientation; if glyphs were ambiguous (mirror/rotation), out.txt names the chosen orientation and rationale, and the string is coherent readable text matching the image.

The direction to pursue, chosen after comparing several different options:
<direction>
- Structured metadata-guided extraction with orientation-verified rendering
  Plan: First inspect text.gcode for extrusion-mode (grep M82/M83), layer/object markers (;LAYER_CHANGE, ;Z:, ;HEIGHT:, ; printing object, M486, ;TYPE:) to identify the exact Z-layer/object/feature that is the embossed text, prioritizing named M486/printing-object blocks over generic TYPE:Custom or top-layer heuristics. Write a Python parser that tracks G90/G91 and M82/M83 state independently, computes per-line E delta correctly (line-E if M83, running-total diff with G92 E0 resets if M82), and classifies each G1/G0 line as a printing move only if X and/or Y changes AND E delta > 0, breaking the current polyline into a new segment whenever a travel/retraction/non-printing move interrupts the run. Render all segments for the isolated text region with matplotlib using ax.set_aspect('equal') and no invert_yaxis (preserving native Y-up), saving to text_render.png sized proportionally to the X/Y extents; open and visually inspect the PNG. If the glyphs appear reversed or rotated, systematically re-render with X-flip, Y-flip, and 90/180/270 rotations until a readable orientation is found, then finalize. Write out.txt with the exact text string plus explanation naming the specific Z height/object/TYPE used, the orientation applied, and the observed glyph shapes confirming the reading; verify all acceptance-checklist commands (grep for M82/M83, layer markers, aspect setting, invert_yaxis absence) pass before finishing.
  Risk: The biggest failure mode is misidentifying the E-mode or mishandling G92 E0 resets under M82, causing every extrusion classification to be wrong (either plotting travels as prints or dropping real strokes), which silently produces a garbled or blank image that gets misread as text rather than triggering re-verification against the raw grep output.
</direction>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parse text.gcode, isolate the 'Embossed text' object (M486 S0 blocks),
extract true printing extrusion moves (X/Y change + positive E delta),
and render them to a PNG for visual inspection.
"""
import re
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

GCODE_PATH = "text.gcode"

# --- Step 1: confirm E mode (M82 absolute vs M83 relative) ---
e_mode = None  # 'relative' or 'absolute'
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for line in f:
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("M83"):
            e_mode = "relative"
            break
        if s.startswith("M82"):
            e_mode = "absolute"
            break
print("Detected E mode:", e_mode)
assert e_mode == "relative", "Expected M83 (relative E) per Prusa default"

# --- Step 2: walk the file, track M486 object-selection state, XYZ position,
# and running E (not strictly needed since relative, but track G92 E0 resets anyway) ---

current_object = None   # None = not inside any tracked object block; 0 = "Embossed text" (S0); 1 = "Shape-Box" (S1)
object_names = {}        # index -> name, populated from "M486 A<name>" lines that follow M486 S<index>? Actually names come right after "M486 S<idx>" as "M486 A<name>"

# From the inspection: lines 25-30 define object table:
#   M486 S0
#   M486 AEmbossed text
#   M486 S-1
#   M486 S1
#   M486 AShape-Box
#   M486 S-1
# Then later, "M486 S0" / "M486 S1" / "M486 S-1" switch which object is "active" for subsequent moves.

last_declared_index = None

x = y = z = 0.0
have_xy = False

segments = []       # list of lists of (x,y) points - for the isolated text object
current_seg = []

# feature/type tracking not required (no ;TYPE: comments present in this file)

line_no = 0
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for raw in f:
        line_no += 1
        line = raw.split(";", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        if line.startswith("M486"):
            # M486 S<idx>  -> select object idx as active (or -1 = none)
            # M486 A<name> -> assign name to the most recently declared index
            m = re.match(r"M486\s+S(-?\d+)", line)
            if m:
                idx = int(m.group(1))
                last_declared_index = idx
                current_object = idx if idx != -1 else None
                # a new object block starting -> break any open polyline
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
                continue
            m2 = re.match(r"M486\s+A(.+)", line)
            if m2:
                name = m2.group(1).strip()
                if last_declared_index is not None:
                    object_names[last_declared_index] = name
                continue
            continue

        if not (line.startswith("G0") or line.startswith("G1")):
            continue

        tokens = line.split()
        cmd = tokens[0]
        new_x, new_y, new_z, e_val = None, None, None, None
        for t in tokens[1:]:
            letter = t[0]
            try:
                val = float(t[1:])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if letter == "X":
                new_x = val
            elif letter == "Y":
                new_y = val
            elif letter == "Z":
                new_z = val
            elif letter == "E":
                e_val = val

        prev_x, prev_y = x, y
        moved_xy = False
        if new_x is not None:
            x = new_x
            moved_xy = True
        if new_y is not None:
            y = new_y
            moved_xy = True
        if new_z is not None:
            z = new_z

        is_printing = moved_xy and (e_val is not None) and (e_val > 0)

        # Only collect points while inside object index 0 ("Embossed text")
        if current_object == 0:
            if is_printing:
                if not current_seg:
                    current_seg.append((prev_x, prev_y))
                current_seg.append((x, y))
            else:
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
        else:
            if current_seg:
                segments.append(current_seg)
                current_seg = []

if current_seg:
    segments.append(current_seg)

print("Object names discovered:", object_names)
print("Number of extrusion segments for object 0 (Embossed text):", len(segments))

all_pts = [p for seg in segments for p in seg]
xs = [p[0] for p in all_pts]
ys = [p[1] for p in all_pts]
if not xs:
    raise SystemExit("No points found for the text object - check object index logic")

xmin, xmax = min(xs), max(xs)
ymin, ymax = min(ys), max(ys)
print(f"X extent: {xmin:.3f} to {xmax:.3f} (span {xmax-xmin:.3f})")
print(f"Y extent: {ymin:.3f} to {ymax:.3f} (span {ymax-ymin:.3f})")
print(f"Total points: {len(all_pts)}")

# --- Step 3: render with matplotlib, equal aspect, Y-up (no invert_yaxis) ---
span_x = max(xmax - xmin, 0.001)
span_y = max(ymax - ymin, 0.001)
fig_w = 12
fig_h = fig_w * (span_y / span_x)
fig_h = max(fig_h, 2)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(fig_w, fig_h), dpi=200)
for seg in segments:
    if len(seg) < 2:
        continue
    sx = [p[0] for p in seg]
    sy = [p[1] for p in seg]
    ax.plot(sx, sy, color="black", linewidth=1.2, solid_capstyle="round")

ax.set_aspect("equal")
margin_x = span_x * 0.05
margin_y = span_y * 0.05
ax.set_xlim(xmin - margin_x, xmax + margin_x)
ax.set_ylim(ymin - margin_y, ymax + margin_y)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("text_render.png", dpi=200, facecolor="white")
print("Saved text_render.png")

Key rules and conventions:
- Coordinates are in millimeters. G21 = mm (essentially always), G20 = inches (never used by PrusaSlicer). All X/Y/Z/E values are floating point mm.
- Positioning modes are INDEPENDENT: G90/G91 control XYZ absolute/relative; M82/M83 control the EXTRUDER (E) absolute/relative. This split is the #1 parse mistake  rom the XYZ mode.

- A PRINTING extrusion move (what to plot) = a G1 (or G0) line that changes X and/or Y AND has a positive E delta. EXCLUDE: pure Z moves, retraction/unretraction (E-only lines with no X/Y), travel moves (X/Y present but E absent or E<=0), and wipe moves.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parse text.gcode, isolate the 'Embossed text' object (M486 S0 blocks),
extract true printing extrusion moves (X/Y change + positive E delta),
and render them to a PNG for visual inspection.
"""
import re
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

GCODE_PATH = "text.gcode"

# --- Step 1: confirm E mode (M82 absolute vs M83 relative) ---
e_mode = None  # 'relative' or 'absolute'
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for line in f:
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("M83"):
            e_mode = "relative"
            break
        if s.startswith("M82"):
            e_mode = "absolute"
            break
print("Detected E mode:", e_mode)
assert e_mode == "relative", "Expected M83 (relative E) per Prusa default"

# --- Step 2: walk the file, track M486 object-selection state, XYZ position,
# and running E (not strictly needed since relative, but track G92 E0 resets anyway) ---

current_object = None   # None = not inside any tracked object block; 0 = "Embossed text" (S0); 1 = "Shape-Box" (S1)
object_names = {}        # index -> name, populated from "M486 A<name>" lines that follow M486 S<index>? Actually names come right after "M486 S<idx>" as "M486 A<name>"

# From the inspection: lines 25-30 define object table:
#   M486 S0
#   M486 AEmbossed text
#   M486 S-1
#   M486 S1
#   M486 AShape-Box
#   M486 S-1
# Then later, "M486 S0" / "M486 S1" / "M486 S-1" switch which object is "active" for subsequent moves.

last_declared_index = None

x = y = z = 0.0
have_xy = False

segments = []       # list of lists of (x,y) points - for the isolated text object
current_seg = []

# feature/type tracking not required (no ;TYPE: comments present in this file)

line_no = 0
with open(GCODE_PATH) as f:
    for raw in f:
        line_no += 1
        line = raw.split(";", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue

        if line.startswith("M486"):
            # M486 S<idx>  -> select object idx as active (or -1 = none)
            # M486 A<name> -> assign name to the most recently declared index
            m = re.match(r"M486\s+S(-?\d+)", line)
            if m:
                idx = int(m.group(1))
                last_declared_index = idx
                current_object = idx if idx != -1 else None
                # a new object block starting -> break any open polyline
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
                continue
            m2 = re.match(r"M486\s+A(.+)", line)
            if m2:
                name = m2.group(1).strip()
                if last_declared_index is not None:
                    object_names[last_declared_index] = name
                continue
            continue

        if not (line.startswith("G0") or line.startswith("G1")):
            continue

        tokens = line.split()
        cmd = tokens[0]
        new_x, new_y, new_z, e_val = None, None, None, None
        for t in tokens[1:]:
            letter = t[0]
            try:
                val = float(t[1:])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if letter == "X":
                new_x = val
            elif letter == "Y":
                new_y = val
            elif letter == "Z":
                new_z = val
            elif letter == "E":
                e_val = val

        prev_x, prev_y = x, y
        moved_xy = False
        if new_x is not None:
            x = new_x
            moved_xy = True
        if new_y is not None:
            y = new_y
            moved_xy = True
        if new_z is not None:
            z = new_z

        is_printing = moved_xy and (e_val is not None) and (e_val > 0)

        # Only collect points while inside object index 0 ("Embossed text")
        if current_object == 0:
            if is_printing:
                if not current_seg:
                    current_seg.append((prev_x, prev_y))
                current_seg.append((x, y))
            else:
                if current_seg:
                    segments.append(current_seg)
                    current_seg = []
        else:
            if current_seg:
                segments.append(current_seg)
                current_seg = []

if current_seg:
    segments.append(current_seg)

print("Object names discovered:", object_names)
print("Number of extrusion segments for object 0 (Embossed text):", len(segments))

all_pts = [p for seg in segments for p in seg]
xs = [p[0] for p in all_pts]
ys = [p[1] for p in all_pts]
if not xs:
    raise SystemExit("No points found for the text object - check object index logic")

xmin, xmax = min(xs), max(xs)
ymin, ymax = min(ys), max(ys)
print(f"X extent: {xmin:.3f} to {xmax:.3f} (span {xmax-xmin:.3f})")
print(f"Y extent: {ymin:.3f} to {ymax:.3f} (span {ymax-ymin:.3f})")
print(f"Total points: {len(all_pts)}")

# --- Step 3: render with matplotlib, equal aspect, Y-up (no invert_yaxis) ---
span_x = max(xmax - xmin, 0.001)
span_y = max(ymax - ymin, 0.001)
fig_w = 12
fig_h = fig_w * (span_y / span_x)
fig_h = max(fig_h, 2)

margin_x = span_x * 0.05
margin_y = span_y * 0.05
ax.set_xlim(xmin - margin_x, xmax + margin_x)
ax.set_ylim(ymin - margin_y, ymax + margin_y)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("text_render.png", dpi=200, facecolor="white")

messages.content:
You are an expert software engineer. Solve the task by writing and running real code with your tools.

- The deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output, not a description. Actually run and exercise what you build.
- Match the output contract exactly: the requested filename, path, format, and fields. Follow the task's stated whitespace and trailing-newline requirement precisely, whether it asks for one or forbids one. A near-miss fails.
- When an exact check decides success (a numeric tolerance, an exact match, or a hidden test), list the judgment calls you made — each place the task could be read two ways. Check your solution once under each reading. When it passes under all of them, you are done: submit. Re-running a check that already passed adds no information, and every extra minute spent re-verifying a correct answer is worse than submitting it. If you find yourself checking the same property twice, stop and submit.
- If a tool call fails because an argument was malformed or invalid, the environment has not changed — no files moved, no directory disappeared. Fix the argument and retry. Never go searching for "lost" files because one call failed.
- Call `saveDraft` as you go, whenever you finish a meaningful step: the files you have written so far, what you verified, what is left. Your run has a cost and time budget, and if it runs out mid-task the most recent draft is what the caller receives. A run that saved nothing returns nothing.
- For a task with more than two steps, call `todoWrite` first and mark each item done the moment it is finished.
- You have web search. Use it when a task needs current or external information rather than guessing or declining.
- NEVER fabricate output you did not actually produce.

## Avoid bash and exec when possible
